slides.text:
Advantages of compiled & interpreted languages
• Advantages of compiled languages
• Faster performance due to translation to machine code in advance
• Opportunity to apply quite powerful optimizations during the compile stage
• Advantages of interpreted languages
• Easier to implement (writing good compilers is very hard)
• No need to run a compilation stage: can execute code directly on-the-fly
• Better suited for dynamic languages due to on-the-fly code changes and immediate feedback

slides.text:
Syntax tree
• Tree representation of the syntactic structure of text (often source code) written in a formal language
• Each node of the tree denotes a construct in the text
• The syntax is abstract: it does not represent every detail, but just the structural or content-related details
• For example: grouping parentheses are implicit in the tree structure, so these do not have to be represented as separate nodes
• A syntactic construct like if-else statement may be denoted by means of a single node with e.g. three branches
• Used in compilers, program analysis and program transformation systems

Motivation for syntax trees
Widely used in compilers to represent the program
Usually the result of the syntax analysis phase of a compiler
Serve as an intermediate representation of the program
Have a strong impact on the final output of the compiler
Properties
Can be edited and enhanced with information such as properties and annotations
Do not need to include inessential punctuation or delimiters
Contain extra information about the program
Example: store the position in the source code to print useful messages
